warmdown.name: Warm-down — Sprints in age groups (8 min, every week)
warmdown.setup: Lanes marked with cones. Distance by age: 3-4yrs 15m, 5yrs 20m, 6yrs 25-30m.
warmdown.how: Children run in their age group, three or four at a time, two runs each. Every child is named and cheered as they cross. Run THROUGH the line, not to it. This is the same every week and that is the point — they get to feel themselves getting faster.
warmdown.adaptation: 15m, running toward a coach with open arms. Two runs, not three.
warmdown.watchFor: Slowing down before the line. Put a cone 3m past the finish and ask them to run to that one.

rules: No separate warm-up — the Game rotation IS the warm-up. Go straight in.
Each series runs two weeks: the same four rotations both weeks, a fresh game the second week.
Warm-down is the same every week: sprints in age groups, two runs each, every child named and cheered.
Never rank children against each other. Each child beats their own cone.
Beanbags before balls. Foam before real. No rigid hurdles, no real discus, no high jump mats at this age.
3-4 year olds: success first — make the task small enough that they succeed, then grow it.

series.name: Finding our feet
series.coachNote: First series — names before anything else. Walk the boundary cones with them on day one, then keep the same boundaries for both weeks so week two feels familiar.

cues: Run tall — head still, eyes forward
Arms bent at 90 degrees, swinging front to back not across
Knees lift forward
Land on the ball of the foot, light and quiet
Run THROUGH the finish line, not to it
rotations.adaptation: Walk and jog only. Stay near a coach. Two calls maximum — green and red.
rotations.watchFor: Children watching the floor instead of the space. Cue 'eyes up'.
rotations.backup: Fast Cars — run laps, change gear on call

cues: Face the target
Step forward with the OPPOSITE foot
Swing the arm low and straight, like a pendulum
Let go at the front
Point at the target after you let go
rotations.adaptation: Throw from 1m into a hoop on the floor, two hands. Success first.
rotations.watchFor: Throwing with the same foot forward as the throwing arm. Chalk a footprint.
rotations.backup: Toy Basketball — throw into the high hoop

cues: Bend the knees into a crouch

series.name: Catch and jump
series.coachNote: Never rank the jumps. Each child marks their own landing with their own cone, and in week two they try to beat the cone they set in week one.

cues: Bend knees into a crouch

rotations.backup: Jump and Reach — jump up to touch a held target

cues: Watch the ball all the way in

rotations.backup: Scarf Pop — toss a scarf high, clap once, catch

series.name: Throw it far

finalNight.name: Mini meet + prizegiving
finalNight.description: No normal rotations. Children visit each of the four stations as a fun 'meet' — long jump (beat your own cone), high jump (scissor over a low elastic), hurdles (foam, step and run) and relays (everyone runs, no winner). Parents are invited for the last twenty minutes. Every child is named, cheered and handed a certificate individually. Finish with Parachute Games.
stations: Long jump — beat your own cone from the season
High jump — scissor over a low elastic (never rope)
Hurdles — foam hurdles, step and run
Relays — everyone runs, announce when every team finishes
finalNight.equipment: 30 cones, long jump mat or sandpit, 1 low elastic, 8 foam hurdles, 12 beanbags, bibs, Parachute, 10 soft balls, certificates
